mission: Find and fix the root cause of the intermittent failure of test_apply_discount in checkout-service, so the team can trust CI again. A fix that only hides the flakiness is a failure: if the non-determinism comes from production code, fix it there.
provisions: - Repo: [REPO PATH]. Service code: services/checkout/. Test: tests/test_discounts.py. - Run the single test: [TEST COMMAND] -k test_apply_discount - Run the full suite: [FULL SUITE COMMAND] - CI logs of recent failures: [LOG LOCATION OR CI LINK] - Read files as you need them; do not load the whole repository up front.
order_of_operations: 1. Reproduce: run the test repeatedly (at least 50 runs) and record the failure rate before changing anything. 2. Isolate: identify the source of non-determinism (e.g. ordering, time, shared state, concurrency, randomness, external calls) and confirm it with a targeted experiment. 3. Fix at the root, in test or production code as the evidence indicates. 4. Verify (see success_spec), then write the PR description. Pause and report after step 2 if the root cause is in production code and the fix would change customer-facing pricing behavior.

template.note: Format only. Do not reuse its content.

anchors.template: ## Root cause [One paragraph: what was non-deterministic and why.] ## Fix [What changed, in which files, and why this addresses the root cause.] ## Evidence [Failure rate before: X/50. After: Y/N runs. Full suite: pass/fail.] ## Not verified [Anything you could not check.]

scope: - Do not add retries, sleeps, skips, or xfail markers, and do not loosen assertions. - Change only files needed for the fix; no unrelated refactors or dependency upgrades. - If you cannot reproduce the failure in 200 runs, stop and report what you tried.
success_spec: Done means all of the following are true and reported: 1. The test passes in at least 200 consecutive runs after the fix. 2. The full suite passes. 3. The PR description follows the template, including the "Not verified" section. Return: the branch name, the PR description, and the before/after failure rates.
